criterion: no plan with the shortest central flights the triangle inequality allows lies inside a forest gap (L < E) and costs less than E (0 counterexamples); a targeted search, not a proof
explanation: 231 of 100,000 instances have a forest gap; on the 231 the exhaustive search finished, 255 gaps were tested and 0 contain a plan cheaper than E. A targeted search on tiny instances, independent of the written proof of Theorem 4.4.
hypothesis: Theorem 4.4 (Conjecture 4.10 of revision 2): under (S) and (AΔ), without (A1), every plan is still weakly dominated by an admissible partition. A counterexample can only sit in a gap where L < E.

sizes.instances: 100,000 random symmetric instances, n in 2..3, p in 2..3, t in p+1..6, d sorted in [1,9], c in [1,30]
sizes.truth: central flights |d_a - d_b|, up to s+2 landings, timeout 900 s
